correctness.rationale: For a red edge uv, exactly two of its four adjacent edges must be red, giving a_u+a_v=4 for red incidence degrees a_v; for a blue edge the count gives a_u+a_v=2. All edges stay inside the profile classes {1,3} or {0,2}, and connectedness forces one class. Each profile-3 vertex is adjacent only to profile-1 vertices, each profile-1 vertex has exactly one such neighbor: D of profile-3 vertices is an efficient dominating set. The other class is its color swap. Conversely any efficient dominating set yields precisely two strong-majority assignments, so b=2p and |V| divisible by four for existence. The 2-power vertex-transitive and Möbius cases use the explicitly quoted previously published Knor–Potočnik Theorem 1.2 and Lemma 2.2; an even Hamiltonian-cycle/chord proper 3-edge coloring supplies index 3 when no code. Independent brute-force graph checks verified K4 (4 codes,8 assignments), K3,3 (0,0), square prism (4,8), directly applying the original edge-neighbor condition.

value.rationale: An exact global structural equivalence for a newly studied edge-coloring invariant across all connected cubic graphs, including exact labeled multiplicity, transfers substantial older perfect-code classifications and exposes the Möbius obstruction. It is more than recomputing known prism counts.

final_claim: For any connected simple cubic graph G, the number of two-named-colour strong-majority edge assignments equals twice the number of efficient dominating vertex sets (perfect 1-codes), with a canonical two-to-one correspondence; known perfect-code classification implies the complete 2-power-order vertex-transitive cubic index classification and b(M_t)=8 iff t≡2 (mod4), else 0.
limitations: Restricted to finite nonempty connected simple cubic graphs with named 2-color palette.
When no efficient dominating set exists, the theorem does not determine the graph’s index beyond excluding two colors.
